{{Short description|Chinese mathematician}}
{{For|the Chinese magnetic resonance imaging scientist|Xin Zhou (MRI scientist)}}
'''Xin Zhou''' is a mathematician known for his contributions in [[scattering theory]], [[integrable system]]s, [[random matrices]] and [[Riemann–Hilbert problem]]s.

He is Professor Emeritus of Mathematics at [[Duke University]]. Zhou had obtained M.Sc. from the [[University of the Chinese Academy of Sciences]] in 1982 and then got his Ph.D. in 1988 from the [[University of Rochester]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://math.duke.edu/people/xin-zhou|title=Xin Zhou|access-date=2019-01-29|publisher=Duke University}}</ref> He received the [[Pólya Prize (SIAM)|Pólya prize]] in 1998<ref>{{cite web|title=Mathematics People|date=October 1998|url=http://www.ams.org/notices/199810/people.pdf|publisher=[[American Mathematics Society]]|access-date=2012-09-06|archive-date=2016-03-04|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304064913/http://www.ams.org/notices/199810/people.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref> and was awarded with the Guggenheim Fellowship in 1999.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gf.org/fellows/all-fellows/xin-zhou/|title=Xin Zhou|publisher=Guggenheim Foundation|access-date=2019-01-29|archive-date=2019-04-21|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190421234519/https://www.gf.org/fellows/all-fellows/xin-zhou/|url-status=dead}}</ref> He is most well known for his work with [[Percy Deift]] on the steepest descent method for oscillatory Riemann–Hilbert problems.<ref>{{cite journal|jstor=2946540|title=A Steepest Descent Method for Oscillatory Riemann--Hilbert Problems. Asymptotics for the MKdV Equation|author1=Deift, P.|author2=Zhou, X.|date=1 January 1993|journal=Annals of Mathematics|volume=137|issue=2|pages=295–368|doi=10.2307/2946540|arxiv=math/9201261|s2cid=12699956 }}</ref>
